title: Liskov Substitution Violations at Serialization Boundaries
pattern: Representing polymorphic inheritance or choice structures at boundaries where certain variants lack semantic properties or violate subtype expectations.
why_bad: It causes serialization failures and runtime crashes when downstream processors receive a valid subclass/variant that cannot fulfill the structural contract.
detection: Deserializers mapping enums or polymorphic constructs where certain variants trigger panics or return empty errors during downstream map processing.
counterexample: Purely algebraic data types handled exhaustively in local pattern matching. Mark as `Context-dependent`.
fix: Ensure all variants serialized across boundaries satisfy the substitution contract, or use explicit, flat union representations.
source: *Practical Object-Oriented Design* by Sandi Metz (Liskov Substitution Principle at boundaries, p. 125).
